397.title: Additions [on the 'Poalei Zion' Press]
397.summary: A sharply critical essay surveys the style, content and political tone of Poalei Zion party journals and collected writings in Palestine.

1430.title: The Two Teachers
1430.summary: A humorous narrative portrays two itinerant Hasidic tutors, experts in grammar and logic, their livelihoods, beliefs, and quiet skepticism about contemporary rabbis.

1775.title: In Rebellious Discourse
1775.summary: An argumentative essay analyzes discriminatory limits on Jewish civil servants and questions whether personal resignation is preferable to organized political struggle.

2066.title: In the Iron Carriage
2066.summary: A first-person train journey narrative presents a sharp dialog between a freethinking adult and a devout youth fleeing work to study Torah.

3240.title: Peretz Smolenskin on “Vengeance of the Covenant”
3240.summary: An essay analyzes the nationalist testament-like story, its historical background, aims for Jewish youth, and Smolenskin’s own account of its creation.

3692.title: The Crown of the Head
3692.summary: A humorous moral tale in elevated, fairy-tale style about a gloomy overthinker who fantasizes about repairing people like broken clocks.

4261.title: “Ha-Tsefirah” and Its Editor Nahum Sokolow
4261.summary: An essay marking the jubilee of a Hebrew newspaper, assessing its cultural role and celebrating the literary originality of Nahum Sokolow.

4413.title: There
4413.summary: An essay reflects on changing meanings of diaspora and Israel, the Holocaust’s devastation, and the possibility of consolation and future Jewish continuity.

4546.title: First Sanctity and Second Sanctity
4546.summary: Analytical rabbinic essay that examines Talmudic and Maimonidean views on the Land of Israel’s sanctity in the first and second returns.

4741.title: Legends of the Red Jews
4741.summary: A prose introduction describing Benjamin’s wondrous journeys to the hidden land of the Red Jews and the cryptic legends derived from them.

5668.title: In the National Council
5668.summary: An essayistic political critique describes the third session of the Jewish National Council in Palestine and its struggle for real autonomous power.

5878.title: The Kollelim and the General Committee
5878.summary: A polemical essay discusses disputes among Jerusalem charity associations over the collection and distribution of funds to different communities.

5901.title: The Ten Commandments
5901.summary: A reflective essay that questions and interprets the commandment “You shall not covet,” distinguishing types of desire and their moral value for individuals and the Jewish people.

5910.title: Judah Leib Katzenelson (Buki ben Yigli)
5910.summary: A literary-critical biographical essay presents Katzenelson’s work in scientific Hebrew, his stories and legends, and his influence on Hebrew culture.

6180.title: The Writers’ Association and Its Newspaper
6180.summary: An oratorical essay to the renewed Hebrew Writers’ Association reflects on modern Hebrew literature’s growth and its cultural responsibility to the public.

6217.title: Until When Did They Speak Hebrew? Part H: The Language in the Temple
6217.summary: Analyzes Talmudic and historical evidence about whether Hebrew or Aramaic was spoken in the Temple and when any linguistic shift occurred.

7743.title: Marxism
7743.summary: A reflective personal essay recounting early days of field labor in a moshava and an incongruous lecture against Marxism amid physical hardship.

7845.title: The Question of Education
7845.summary: An essay that analyzes why Jews in Jerusalem resist modern schools and secular enlightenment, contrasting Jewish and missionary approaches to education.

7871.title: And Mendele the Elder
7871.summary: A reflective prose sketch portrays an aged Hebrew writer at his jubilee, his undimmed creative powers, his plans, and his lively presence.

8123.title: On the Second Anniversary of the Mandate’s Confirmation
8123.summary: An analytical Zionist political essay evaluates the British Mandate for Palestine and the Jewish national home two years after its approval.

9600.title: The Devil Dances
9600.summary: A contemplative first-person encounter with Ashmedai, who vividly describes his rule over human corruption, violence, and moral decay on earth.

10140.title: Peace Be Upon You
10140.summary: An essayistic memorial portrait analyzes Sholem Aleichem’s unique Jewish humor, his boundless laughter, and its relation to exile, suffering, and creativity.

10577.title: The Tale of Prince Florizel and the Secret Police
10577.summary: A prince in Paris struggles over a cursed diamond's fate, advising a repentant priest as intrigue and police danger gather around him.

10814.title: The Will of the Nation
10814.summary: A reflective prose account recalls an 1891 exploratory journey in the Haifa–Acre valley to purchase land for Jewish settlement and its moral challenge.

10963.title: At the Council of “HeHalutz” in Danzig
10963.summary: A Zionist labor leader addresses a HeHalutz council about movement crises, vocational versus pioneering training, and the need for deep Hebrew cultural work.

11266.title: For the Turn of the Year
11266.summary: The essay reviews the outgoing year’s wars, persecutions, economic crises and Jewish suffering, contrasting them with emerging Zionist aspirations and renewal.

11441.title: Three Who Ate
11441.summary: A reflective first-person narrative recounts a remembered incident where three revered community leaders publicly eat on Yom Kippur in the synagogue.

11504.title: In Honor of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
11504.summary: On the eve of Lag BaOmer, two boys argue about collecting wood for the bonfire and whether taking others’ wood is stealing.

11505.title: Friends
11505.summary: A simple schoolroom story in prose follows two young boys whose quarrel over a ball and a promised kite tests their friendship.

11517.title: Name Change
11517.summary: A shy new immigrant boy in a Hebrew school is teased by classmates and questioned by the teacher about his foreign-sounding name.

13309.title: Dr. Yosef Sapir
13309.summary: An admiring biographical essay portrays a veteran Zionist activist’s lifelong, selfless public work, dedication, and modest character on his sixtieth birthday.

13918.title: Ze'ev Latski-Bertoldi
13918.summary: Biographical-political sketch tracing Zeev Latski-Bertoldi's upbringing, Zionist-socialist convictions, underground activism, and role in early Poalei Zion circles in Russia.

16212.title: The Letter
16212.summary: A young Hebrew teacher receives a devastating letter that shatters his plans to teach and build a life with his beloved.

16905.title: The Poet’s Recompense
16905.summary: A narrative poem recounts a legendary Persian poet of light and love, his inspired hymns, and the unjust reward from his ruler.

17249.title: The Drop of Water
17249.summary: A magician examines a drop of water under a magnifying glass and sees countless tiny creatures behaving like a quarrelsome human city.

17929.title: Conversation in the Yeshiva Above: A Vision
17929.summary: An elevated visionary prose dialogue in heaven where allegorical figures discuss a revered Jewish scholar’s jubilee and his defense of faithful Judaism.

19078.title: The Fastidious One
19078.summary: A meticulous young accountant with extreme aesthetic sensitivity and horror of ugliness struggles with loneliness when a physically unappealing young woman lodges opposite him.

20421.title: Uncle Rabbi Yitzhak
20421.summary: A family memoir recounts complex marriages, rabbinic figures, and the rise and downfall of a sharp merchant uncle in 19th‑century Russia.

20425.title: A Dispute “For the Sake of Heaven”
20425.summary: A nostalgic memoiristic sketch recounts a fierce, often comic synagogue struggle between Ashkenazi and Chabad prayer rites in a small town.

20924.title: A Candle for an Hour Burns All Night
20924.summary: A narrative prose story follows a gifted boy devoted to Torah study whose nighttime learning against his father’s worries leads to his mysterious disappearance.

21349.title: Astarte in the Nethermost Sheol
21349.summary: A mythic narrative poem recounting Astarte’s threatened, ritual-laden descent through the gates of the underworld to her sister Ereshkigal.

22624.title: Without a Nose
22624.summary: A cheerful noseless boy discovers his difference, suffers mockery, and undertakes a magical quest to obtain a normal nose.

22625.title: Bela
22625.summary: A simple didactic story in plain prose about a mischievous, lazy, stubborn boy and the devotion of his poor parents.

22627.title: The Wise Man’s Secret
22627.summary: A poor, reclusive scholar devotes his life to study and nature while secretly seeking a way to save humanity from diseases.

22642.title: What Ails You, My Only One?
22642.summary: An exhortative devotional poem addresses the soul, urging it to detach from worldly life, endure exile, and trust in God’s protection.

22811.title: The Sorrow and Threats of Mr. M. M.
22811.summary: A polemical political essay critiques a journalist’s portrayal of internal debates in the Jewish workers’ movement over cooperation with Revisionist labor.

23216.title: The Power of Perseverance
23216.summary: Essay reflecting on twenty‑five years of Degania, portraying pioneering Jewish agricultural labor and the birth of a new collective social ideal in Palestine.

24753.title: Instead of a Sermon – A Play
24753.summary: A family and friends discuss a boy’s upcoming bar mitzvah sermon, debating memorized lofty words versus simple, heartfelt speech.

30793.title: The Children in Cyprus
30793.summary: A documentary-style prose account depicts Jewish refugee children in a Cyprus camp organizing their own youth village, studies, and cultural life amid exile.

31648.title: In Steep Mountains I Walked…
31648.summary: A reflective lyric poem follows a restless soul who flees the city to seek eternal divine beauty and hidden mystery in the mountains.

31697.title: On the Periodical “Voices”: In the Bosom of Holiness
31697.summary: An introspective essay that, from autumnal solitude, meditates on a spiritual journal’s discussions of suffering, faith, holiness, and life’s purpose.

33037.title: The Book Tahkemoni – Gate Forty-Two
33037.summary: A rhymed narrative debate contrasts miserliness and generosity through elevated speeches among wise men and nobles in ornate Hebrew.

36691.title: From His Letters
36691.summary: An introductory memoir presents the humane relationship and four-year correspondence between Vladimir Korolenko and the young Jewish writer Nahum Cohen, outlining Cohen’s life and suffering.

37670.title: Storm-Tossed Ship
37670.summary: An essay reflects on a pioneering Jewish-owned passenger ship, its economic struggle and sale, and the Zionist institutions’ failure to support Hebrew maritime enterprise.

41558.title: Prayer for Peace
41558.summary: A liturgical-style Hebrew poem prays for lasting world peace, thanks for the war’s end and Balfour Declaration, and mercy for suffering Jews.

41669.title: The Man
41669.summary: A boy builds a snow figure on the first night of Hanukkah and returns home as his family lights the holiday candles.

42005.title: Love
42005.summary: A reflective philosophical essay explores the nature of love, its development across ages, and its profound role in human life and society.

43298.title: Jacob Bukshtain
43298.summary: A biographical-essay portrait of a modest Zionist activist from a Hasidic Ukrainian background who becomes deeply involved in Russian Zionist life and plans immigration to Palestine.

43413.title: Europe
43413.summary: A first-person travel diary records a 1946 journey via Cairo, mixing everyday impressions with reflections on politics, society, and Jewish–Arab relations.

44011.title: The Factors in the Spread of Tuberculosis in the Land of Israel
44011.summary: A medical essay in formal Hebrew explains forms of tuberculosis, modes of infection, and conditions affecting its spread in the Land of Israel.

45475.title: Positive
45475.summary: A satirical essay that flips common complaints to highlight contradictions and hypocrisies in Israeli politics, society, and Jewish-Arab relations.

46213.title: Is There Another Dish?
46213.summary: A humorous folk-style narrative tells of Ibn Ezra as a poor guest testing a couple’s trust in divine providence and communal respect.

51306.title: For the Improvement of Our Internal Relations
51306.summary: An essay analyzing changing relations within the Zionist Yishuv, criticizing partisan polemics and journalism, and calling for solidarity and responsible political cooperation.

51893.title: Notus and Protus
51893.summary: A humorous first-person monologue recounts how a voracious meat-eater is persuaded toward vegetarianism, relating this downfall from a prison cell.

52747.title: Lakish the Robber (a Tale)
52747.summary: A narrator among children debates books versus heartfelt stories and confronts a boy who proudly admits killing flies out of envy.

52755.title: The Man (A Tale)
52755.summary: A Hanukkah-time story in elevated prose about a boy who builds a snow figure and wonders about bringing it to life through sacred words.

57696.title: Journey in the Land of Romania [Late 1878–Early 1879]
57696.summary: A Hebrew memoiristic travelogue that depicts Jewish life in Romanian cities, antisemitism, and the activities of enlightened Jews and their institutions.

59044.title: The Mission of the Serpent
59044.summary: A rabbinic tale in elevated Hebrew prose where a sage encounters a heaven-sent serpent and tries to divert it after a sinner repents.

59046.title: Cast Your Bread
59046.summary: A didactic folk tale in rabbinic-style prose tells of a man obeying a biblical verse, a growing fish, and the sea creatures’ king.

59092.title: The Frankincense Tree
59092.summary: A fairy-tale prose narrative follows a rich couple’s longed-for child, the mother’s death, a burial under a tree, and a new stepfamily.

59120.title: The Juniper Tree
59120.summary: A literary fairy tale in elevated biblical-style prose narrates a longed-for child’s birth, the mother’s death, and ensuing family events.

63478.title: Why
63478.summary: A reflective first-person psychological sketch portrays a deeply suffering, distrustful woman as the narrator observes her appearance, manner, and inner turmoil.

63577.title: Rudi
63577.summary: A first-person reminiscence depicts a sudden village friendship with a disabled boy, exploring wordless communication, compassion, and emotional closeness.

65124.title: Cities of Greenery
65124.summary: An essay that contrasts real and imagined garden cities while analyzing workers’ suburban settlements around industrial centers and their social-economic roots.

65175.title: Green Cities
65175.summary: The essay analyzes garden-city style workers’ settlements near industrial centers, contrasting idealized plans with economic reality and urban overcrowding.
